page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Lattice enthalpy: the energy required to
completely separate one mole of a solid
ionic compound into its gaseous ions.
Ex: the lattice enthalpy of NaCl is
steps.why: The definition fixes both the amount (one mole) and the end state (separate gaseous ions) — without those two conditions the energy value is not defined.
common_mistakes: Ending at separate atoms. The lattice breaks into IONS, and they must be gaseous.
Leaving out one mole, which the unit kJ mol⁻¹ depends on.
steps.memory_tip: One mole of crystal taken apart into gas-phase ions — that energy is the lattice enthalpy.
steps.margin_note: The NaCl value 788 kJ mol⁻¹ is the standard quoted example.

steps.label: What a high value indicates

lines.text: High lattice enthalpy → a more stable ionic solid

lines: The ions are held more strongly in the
crystal, so more energy is needed to
steps.why: Lattice enthalpy measures the strength of the electrostatic attraction holding the ions in the crystal, so a larger value directly means a more strongly bound, more stable solid.
common_mistakes: Reading a high value as easier to dissolve. A high lattice enthalpy makes the lattice HARDER to take apart.
steps.memory_tip: Bigger energy to break it means it was held more strongly.
